label: LIVE CLAUDE

messages_in.content:
TASK
Propose 3 distinct stress scenarios over a horizon of at most 30 days in which the book below loses at least $5,000,000 (a loss means negative total P&L).
Driver family: cold_snap
Season: winter


INPUTS

   "loses_when": "the WEST on-peak price is below K1",

  },

   "channel": "congestion",
   "gains_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens above c0",
   "loses_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread narrows below c0",
   "position": "P2",
   "what": "Long 25 MW of the N.Y.C. minus WEST price spread around the clock (24 h), strike c0 = 11.60 $/MWh"
  },
  {
   "channel": "dart",
   "gains_when": "real-time clears below day-ahead",
   "loses_when": "real-time clears above day-ahead (real-time spikes)",
   "position": "P3",
   "what": "Receives (day-ahead minus real-time) at WEST off-peak on 50 MW (8 h, 24 h on weekends and holidays)"
  },
  {
   "channel": "gas",
   "gains_when": "the WEST on-peak price rises relative to gas",
   "loses_when": "scenario losses are measured against the unshocked path (the premium cancels), so P4 loses only when its payoff falls BELOW the unshocked payoff, i.e. when gas rises more than power; it can never lose more than that base payoff",
   "position": "P4",
   "what": "Long heat-rate call on 50 MW, on-peak: pays max(WEST on-peak - 8 x gas - 3, 0) minus a premium of 8.29 $/MWh (fair value on the fit sample)"
  },
  {
   "channel": "zone_volume",
   "gains_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread narrows",
   "loses_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens; the loss also grows with load above normal",
   "position": "P5",

  },
  {
   "channel": "tail",
   "gains_when": "the WEST on-peak daily average stays below K6",
   "loses_when": "the WEST on-peak daily average exceeds K6 (price spikes)",
   "position": "P6",
   "what": "Short call on 25 MW of the WEST on-peak daily average, strike K6 = 149.31 $/MWh, premium received 0.53 $/MWh (fair value on the fit sample)"
  }
 ],
 "book_summary": "P1 (when its size is positive) and P4 are LONG WEST power, so higher WEST prices make them GAIN (a negative P1 size is a SHORT swap that loses when WEST rises); higher gas lowers P4. CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: A cold snap raises N.Y.C. load to 1.10 times normal and gas by 40%, while a transmission-constrained import pattern widens the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread by $250/MWh for 10 days. WEST on-peak prices are left unchanged, so the long WEST positions P1 and P4 gain little. The short N.Y.C. retail obligation P5 (140 MW scaled by load) absorbs the widened spread, and P2 offsets only a small part. Losses are estimated by scaling the 5-day winter sensitivities linearly to 10 days, which is an extrapolation and may overstate or understate the result. The Winter Storm Elliott spread analogue supports the size of the congestion channel.

The short N.Y.C. retail position P5 is the main source of loss, and P2 partly offsets it. This scenario tests a slow congestion drain rather than a sharp spike. The 30-day loss is an extrapolation of the 5-day winter sensitivities and carries substantial model uncertainty.

A severe six-day cold snap pushes N.Y.C. peak load to 1.20 times normal and gas up 30%, while the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $300/MWh. This is a sharper, shorter event that concentrates the zone-volume channel on the short retail obligation P5. WEST on-peak prices are unchanged, so the long WEST positions P1 and P4 add little offset. The loss is driven mainly by P5 and partly offset by P2. The result is an extrapolation from the 5-day winter sensitivities and may differ from a full simulation.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

Gas rises 15% on the same days, which lifts the cost base but leaves WEST on-peak prices unchanged, so P1 and P4 add little. The short N.Y.C. retail position P5 carries most of the loss, and P2 partly offsets it. The cumulative spread-days and load effect drive the estimate, which is an extrapolation of the winter sensitivities and carries material uncertainty.

A five-day severe cold snap drives N.Y.C. peak load to 1.20 times normal and widens the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread by $240/MWh, close to the scale of the Winter Storm Elliott spread observation. A $2/MMBtu New York gas basis charge also reduces the heat-rate call P4 payoff, adding a small loss on top of the zone-volume channel. WEST on-peak prices and DART are unchanged, so the book loses mainly through P5, partly offset by P2. The loss is an extrapolation from the 5-day winter sensitivities and is sized to sit just above the $5M target.

scenario.narrative: A sustained heat dome covers the Northeast for 30 days. Zone J (N.Y.C.) load runs about 10% above a typical summer day, and import and transmission limits into the pocket hold the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread about $75/MWh wider than normal. WEST on-peak prices are assumed flat, so the reference price and gas do not move. The shock hits P5, the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail obligation, which loses roughly $3,180/day per $/MWh of spread widening. P2's congestion long offsets only about $600/day per $/MWh. Net loss is estimated at about $5.8M. Engine sensitivities are linear and from a 5-day base, so the 30-day scaling is an assumption.

scenario.narrative: Heat builds in N.Y.C. while upstate WEST prices soften because of high hydro, solar and wind output and weak upstate demand. Over 30 days the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by about $72/MWh and WEST on-peak prices drop about 10% relative to the base path. Load runs 5% above normal. The spread widening drives the main loss through the short N.Y.C. retail position (P5) and P2 offsets only part of it. The softer WEST price reduces P1, the long WEST swap, and P4, the heat-rate call, which are both long WEST exposure. The combined estimated loss is about $5.2M, with the uncertainty noted in the stated estimate. No analogue fits a WEST price decline, so none is cited.

A shorter but intense heat wave lasts 20 days. N.Y.C. load runs 15% above normal and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread blows out by about $105/MWh on each shocked day because local generation and transmission into the pocket are constrained. WEST prices stay near base and gas is unchanged, so the loss comes almost entirely from the N.Y.C. retail short (P5) net of P2's offset. The shock stays well inside the summer pocket spread ceiling of 363.1 and below the historical maximum of 289.7 once the spread is measured against the 5-day base. Estimated loss is about $5.4M over the 20 shocked days, with the rest of the 30-day horizon at base.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: A compact heat dome drives N.Y.C. daily peak load to about 20% above a typical summer day for 10 consecutive days. Pocket transmission and local generation limits widen the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread by about $120/MWh on each shocked day. WEST on-peak prices and gas stay at base, so the loss comes from the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail obligation (P5), which scales with both load and spread. P2's congestion long offsets only part of the loss. The shock is 10 days, inside the 30-day horizon, and the spread is well inside the summer implausibility ceiling of 363.1. No analogue is cited for the load multiplier because the analogue table has no matching load ratio. Estimated loss is about $5.6M.

Over 30 days, heat is concentrated in N.Y.C. while upstate WEST on-peak prices fall about 40% from base, driven by high hydro, solar and wind output and weak upstate load. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $60/MWh and load runs 8% above normal. The lower WEST price reduces P1, the long WEST on-peak swap, and P4, the heat-rate call, which both lose value as WEST falls. The spread widening hurts P5 the most, and P2 offsets part of that. Gas and DART are held at base, so this scenario isolates the WEST price collapse as a second channel alongside the N.Y.C. retail short. No analogue fits a sustained WEST decline, so none is cited. Estimated loss is about $6.0M.

A short, intense heat wave hits N.Y.C. for 7 days. Daily peak load runs 25% above normal and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $200/MWh on each shocked day, similar to the June 2025 heat event, when N.Y.C. real-time on-peak cleared at 625.5 $/MWh against WEST real-time at 416.5 $/MWh on 24 June. The spread stays below the summer implausibility ceiling of 363.1 and under the historical maximum of 289.7 when measured on the same basis. The loss comes mainly from P5's short retail obligation, scaled by load and spread. P2 gains partly offset it. WEST prices, gas and DART are held at base, so the event isolates the N.Y.C. zone-volume channel over a one-week window. Estimated loss is about $5.5M.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: A heat dome holds over the Northeast for 15 days while transmission into the N.Y.C. pocket is constrained and local generation is unavailable. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $140/MWh on each shocked day. Daily peak load runs at the normal heat-wave level, a load ratio of 1.05, so the retail obligation grows slightly. WEST on-peak prices, gas and DART stay at base. The loss comes from the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail position (P5), with P2's congestion long giving partial offset. The 15-day duration is a constrained-pocket episode, separate from the shorter spike and load-driven cases. Spread and load are inside the summer implausibility ceilings of 363.1 and 1.893. Estimated loss is about $5.4M.

Over 20 days, upstate WEST on-peak prices collapse about 75% from base because of high hydro, solar and wind output and weak upstate load. At the same time the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $65/MWh on each shocked day as the pocket stays short of supply. Load runs at the normal heat-wave ratio of 1.00. The WEST drop hits P1, the long 100 MW WEST swap, and P4, the heat-rate call, because both gain only when WEST rises. The spread widening hits P5, the short N.Y.C. retail obligation, and P2 offsets part of that. Gas and DART are held at base, so this case tests a WEST price collapse as the second loss channel alongside the pocket spread. No analogue fits, so none is cited. Estimated loss is about $5.3M.

A severe, persistent heat wave pushes N.Y.C. daily peak load about 35% above a typical summer day for 12 consecutive days. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $120/MWh on each shocked day as the pocket is short of generation and imports. Load is the main driver here, since the retail obligation scales with load/normal load, so the loss is larger per dollar of spread than in a moderate-load case. WEST on-peak prices, gas and DART are held at base to isolate the zone-volume channel. P2's congestion long gives partial offset. The 12-day duration is a longer load-led episode, distinct from the 7-day and 10-day cases. The load ratio of 1.35 is under the summer implausible ceiling of 1.893. No analogue is cited. Estimated loss is about $5.7M.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: A sustained heat dome holds over the Northeast for 20 consecutive days. N.Y.C. daily peak load runs about 8% above a typical summer day, and transmission into the pocket stays constrained, so the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $100/MWh on every shocked day. WEST on-peak prices, gas and DART are held at base to isolate the zone-volume channel. The loss comes mainly from the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail obligation (P5), which scales with the spread over the full 20 days. P2's congestion long offsets part of the loss. The 20-day duration is longer than the 7-, 10-, 12- and 15-day cases already tested. The spread is inside the summer ceiling of 363.1 and the load ratio is inside the ceiling of 1.893. No analogue fits a 20-day spread episode, so none is cited. Estimated loss is about $5.6M.

Day-ahead prices over-forecast heat-driven load, so real-time clears well below day-ahead across WEST for 18 days. The WEST day-ahead minus real-time gap is therefore negative, which the engine represents as dart_pct of -40. This hits P1, the long 100 MW WEST swap, and P4, the heat-rate call, because both lose value when WEST real-time falls relative to the day-ahead price they were struck against. At the same time the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $90/MWh on each shocked day as the pocket stays short. Load stays at the normal summer ratio of 1.00, so the loss comes from DART and the zone-volume channel together. P2 offsets part of the spread loss. The June 2025 heat event recorded a negative WEST DART gap of -272 $/MWh on 24 June, so the sign pattern is grounded in the analogue. The percent shock here is an engine input and is not the same as the dollar gap. Estimated loss is about $5.3M.

scenario.narrative: A short, extreme heat wave hits N.Y.C. for 9 days. Daily peak load runs about 20% above normal, and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $220/MWh on each shocked day, because local generation is out and imports into the pocket are limited. The spread is below the summer implausibility ceiling of 363.1, though above the historical maximum of 289.7 is not claimed. WEST on-peak prices, gas and DART stay at base, so the event isolates the N.Y.C. zone-volume channel. The loss is dominated by the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail obligation (P5), which scales with both load and spread. P2's congestion long offsets part of the loss. The June 2025 event saw N.Y.C. real-time on-peak at 625.5 $/MWh on 24 June, which supports the scale of the shock. Estimated loss is about $6.0M.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: Day-ahead forecasts over-predict heat-driven N.Y.C. load, so real-time clears well below day-ahead across WEST for 14 consecutive days. The engine input dart_pct of -50 represents a real-time price 50% below day-ahead, which hits the long WEST positions P1 and P4 and reduces the DART receipt in P3. At the same time, pocket transmission stays constrained and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $150/MWh on each shocked day. Daily peak load runs 10% above a typical summer day, so the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail obligation (P5) grows with both spread and load. P2's congestion long offsets only part of the loss. The spread and load are inside the summer implausibility ceilings of 363.1 and 1.893. No analogue is cited because no table entry matches a 14-day DART inversion paired with a spread of this size. Estimated loss is about $6.5M.

Over 25 days, a Henry Hub gas rally of 40% passes into the upstate and pocket marginal cost, while the WEST on-peak price falls about 50% from base because hydro, solar and wind output is high and upstate load is weak. The gas rise lowers the payoff of the heat-rate call P4, and the WEST fall reduces the value of the long 100 MW WEST swap P1. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $90/MWh on each shocked day as the pocket stays short of supply. Load runs 5% above normal. P5, the short N.Y.C. retail obligation, is the largest loss channel, and P2 offsets only part of it. The ny_gas_basis_usd of 1.5 reflects the extra cost of delivered gas into the pocket and affects only P4. The gas, WEST and spread shocks together are inside the summer ceilings. No analogue fits this combination, so none is cited. Estimated loss is about $5.8M.

A severe heat wave hits N.Y.C. for 6 days, with local generation out and imports into the pocket curtailed. Daily peak load runs 30% above a typical summer day, and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $280/MWh on each shocked day. The spread is below the summer implausibility ceiling of 363.1. WEST on-peak prices, gas and DART are held at base, so the event isolates the zone-volume channel without the WEST or gas moves used in the other cases. The loss comes mainly from the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail obligation (P5), which scales with both load and spread over only 6 days. P2's congestion long offsets part of the loss. The June 2025 heat event recorded N.Y.C. real-time on-peak at 625.5 $/MWh on 24 June, which supports the scale of the zone-level stress, though the 280 $/MWh spread is an engine assumption rather than a reported figure. Estimated loss is about $5.2M.

scenario.narrative: Gas supply disruption: a multi-day loss of pipeline deliverability into the N.Y.C. zone (Transco/Iroquois-type constraints, possibly with a cold snap) lifts Henry Hub by 150% for 10 days. The gas squeeze is concentrated in the pocket, so N.Y.C. prices clear well above WEST; pocket_minus_ref_usd of +200 $/MWh widens the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread on every shocked day. That hurts P5, the short N.Y.C. retail obligation hedged only with WEST, which loses about $3,700 per MWh of spread per day on its 140 MW. P2's long spread offsets only a small part. ny_gas_basis_usd of +6 raises the gas cost used by P4 only, reducing its call payoff. Load and WEST on-peak are held neutral so the channel is isolated to the congestion/zone-volume book. Expected book loss is about $6.2M before P4 and rounding effects.

scenario.narrative: Sustained Henry Hub supply shock: a 300% gas price rise persists for 20 days after an extended LNG-export and pipeline outage coincides with a cold pattern. Gas costs flow through to N.Y.C. only partially, but the pocket spread widens by 120 $/MWh each day as the in-city generation fuel supply is short. The loss comes from P5 (short 140 MW N.Y.C., long WEST hedge) and is partly offset by P2. The gas move reduces P4's heat-rate call via the 8x gas term and the ny_gas_basis_usd of +15 adds further pressure to its payoff. Load is raised modestly to 1.10 to reflect the cold weather that accompanies the disruption, which increases the retail obligation. WEST on-peak is not moved separately, so P1 neither gains nor loses materially. Losses accumulate linearly over the 20-day duration.

analogue.source: NYISO analogue table, January 2025 cold (NYISO)

scenario.narrative: Short, intense pocket-only gas squeeze: a 120% Henry Hub rise over 5 days, with a 350 $/MWh widening of the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread, reflects a regional gas-deliverability shortfall that bites hardest in N.Y.C. The spread shock is the dominant driver and is set just below the winter historical maximum of 400.6 $/MWh to stay plausible. Over five days this produces a loss of about $5.4M through P5, net of P2's offset. A small ny_gas_basis_usd of +4 captures the higher gas cost in P4's payoff. Load stays at 1.0 because the shock is supply-side, and WEST on-peak and DART are unchanged, so the book's WEST and real-time exposures do not contribute and the loss is isolated to the congestion channel.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: Pipeline curtailment causes a real-time scarcity regime. Henry Hub rises 200% for 12 days as deliverability into the city falls, and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 180 $/MWh on each shocked day. Real-time clears 200% above day-ahead in WEST, which hurts the short-DART position P3 and lifts WEST on-peak prices, helping the long WEST swap P1. The net effect is that the zone-volume loss on P5 (short 140 MW N.Y.C., hedged long WEST) dominates. The engine's winter sensitivities show P5 losing about $3,700 per MWh of spread per day, which gives roughly $8.0M gross over 12 days. P2 offsets about $1.3M, P1 adds a gain of about $2.0M from the dart-driven WEST move, and P3 loses about $0.9M. Net loss is about $5.6M. Estimates are approximate and extrapolated linearly from 5-day sensitivities. Load is held at 1.0 to isolate the channel.

scenario.narrative: Gas-driven pocket squeeze. Henry Hub triples (+200%) for 15 days because of an LNG-export pull combined with a storage shortfall, and N.Y.C. gas-fired generation is constrained at the margin. The pocket spread widens by 120 $/MWh on each day, which is about 40% of the winter historical maximum of 400.6 $/MWh and so stays plausible. P5 is the main loser: roughly $3,700 per MWh-day gross, or about $6.6M over 15 days. P2's long spread offsets about $1.1M. ny_gas_basis_usd of +8 raises the gas cost in P4's heat-rate call, reducing its payoff by a small amount. The load ratio is held at 1.0 because the shock is supply-side. WEST prices and DART are unchanged, so the loss is isolated to the congestion and zone-volume channel. The estimate is a linear extrapolation from the 5-day winter sensitivity and is uncertain.

analogue.source: NYISO analogue table, Winter Storm Elliott

scenario.narrative: Persistent winter gas shortage over 25 days. Henry Hub rises 100% and stays elevated as storage draws stay heavy through a long cold period. Cold-driven load is raised to 1.15 of normal, which increases the retail obligation through P5. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 90 $/MWh on each shocked day, a moderate level that is well below the 400.6 $/MWh winter historical maximum. Over 25 days P5 loses roughly $3,700 per MWh-day gross, about $8.3M, and P2 offsets about $1.35M. The load increase adds a further loss of a few hundred thousand dollars based on the 5-day winter sensitivity, scaled. ny_gas_basis_usd of +3 reduces P4 slightly. WEST on-peak and DART are unchanged so P1 and P3 do not contribute. Overall loss is about $6.5M. This is the least extreme of the three in per-day terms and the most dependent on the duration assumption, so its uncertainty is higher.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: A short, intense pipeline and storage squeeze into N.Y.C. Henry Hub rises 150% for 6 days, and the in-city gas-fired fleet is constrained at the margin. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 320 $/MWh on each shocked day, close to the 338.5 $/MWh Elliott-type level and below the 503.7 $/MWh winter implausibility threshold. The main loss is on P5, the short 140 MW N.Y.C. retail obligation hedged with a long WEST position, which loses roughly $3,500 per MWh of spread per day, about $6.7M gross over 6 days. P2's long spread offsets about $1.2M, and P1 gains a little from the gas-linked WEST move. ny_gas_basis_usd of +5 lowers the P4 call payoff. Load and WEST on-peak are held neutral so the loss is isolated to the congestion and zone-volume channel. The estimate is a linear extrapolation from the 5-day winter sensitivity and is uncertain by roughly 15%.

scenario.narrative: A prolonged cold-driven gas shortage over 14 days. Henry Hub rises 90% as storage draws stay heavy, and cold weather lifts N.Y.C. peak load to 1.25 of a typical winter day, which enlarges the retail obligation in P5. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 140 $/MWh on each day, a moderate level well below the winter historical maximum of 400.6 $/MWh. Over 14 days P5 loses about $6.9M gross from the spread and about $0.3M from the extra load, and P2 offsets about $1.0M. ny_gas_basis_usd of +4 reduces the P4 call payoff. WEST on-peak and DART are unchanged, so P1 and P3 do not contribute. The load ratio is the main new feature versus the other scenarios. Its effect is taken from the 5-day winter sensitivity, scaled linearly, and is therefore uncertain.

scenario.narrative: A mid-intensity pocket gas squeeze over 8 days. Henry Hub rises 80% on a pipeline maintenance overlap with a cold snap, and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 250 $/MWh on each shocked day, which is about 62% of the winter historical maximum and inside the implausibility threshold. Load rises modestly to 1.10 of normal, adding a small increase in the P5 obligation. P5 loses roughly $5.5M gross from the spread and about $0.2M from load, with about $1.2M offset from the long spread in P2 and a small loss on P4 through the basis term. ny_gas_basis_usd of +2 is the gas-cost adder for P4. WEST on-peak and DART are unchanged. No analogue fits the 250 $/MWh spread over 8 days closely enough, so the analogue field is left blank and confidence is low. The loss estimate is a linear scaling of the winter sensitivities and carries the most uncertainty of the three.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

TASK
Propose 3 distinct stress scenarios over a horizon of at most 30 days in which the book below loses at least $5,000,000 (a loss means negative total P&L).
Driver family: gas_supply
Season: winter


INPUTS
Context (units: prices $/MWh, gas $/MMBtu, power MW, time days):
{
 "active_positions": [
  "P1",
  "P2",
  "P3",
  "P4",
  "P5",
  "P6"
 ],
 "book": [
  {
   "channel": "system",
   "gains_when": "the WEST on-peak price is above K1",
   "loses_when": "the WEST on-peak price is below K1",
   "position": "P1",
   "what": "Long 100 MW swap on the WEST on-peak price, strike K1 = 39.49 $/MWh, 16 h per on-peak weekday"
  },
  {
   "channel": "congestion",
   "gains_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens above c0",
   "loses_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread narrows below c0",
   "position": "P2",
   "what": "Long 25 MW of the N.Y.C. minus WEST price spread around the clock (24 h), strike c0 = 11.60 $/MWh"
  },
  {
   "channel": "dart",
   "gains_when": "real-time clears below day-ahead",
   "loses_when": "real-time clears above day-ahead (real-time spikes)",
   "position": "P3",
   "what": "Receives (day-ahead minus real-time) at WEST off-peak on 50 MW (8 h, 24 h on weekends and holidays)"
  },
  {
   "channel": "gas",
   "gains_when": "the WEST on-peak price rises relative to gas",
   "loses_when": "scenario losses are measured against the unshocked path (the premium cancels), so P4 loses only when its payoff falls BELOW the unshocked payoff, i.e. when gas rises more than power; it can never lose more than that base payoff",
   "position": "P4",
   "what": "Long heat-rate call on 50 MW, on-peak: pays max(WEST on-peak - 8 x gas - 3, 0) minus a premium of 8.29 $/MWh (fair value on the fit sample)"
  },
  {
   "channel": "zone_volume",
   "gains_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread narrows",
   "loses_when": "the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens; the loss also grows with load above normal",
   "position": "P5",
   "what": "Retail load obligation: short 140 MW x (load / normal load) in N.Y.C. at fixed price R = 45.65, hedged by a long WEST position at H = 34.05, 24 h; P&L = (R - N.Y.C. price) + (WEST price - H), times load"
  },
  {
   "channel": "tail",
   "gains_when": "the WEST on-peak daily average stays below K6",
   "loses_when": "the WEST on-peak daily average exceeds K6 (price spikes)",
   "position": "P6",
   "what": "Short call on 25 MW of the WEST on-peak daily average, strike K6 = 149.31 $/MWh, premium received 0.53 $/MWh (fair value on the fit sample)"

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: A pipeline-constrained pocket decouples from upstate. Henry Hub rises 130% for 7 days, but WEST on-peak prices fall 10% because upstate gas is in surplus and gas-fired output there is not constrained. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 280 $/MWh on each day, close to the Elliott-type level of 338.5 $/MWh. P5 loses through the spread, while P1, which is long WEST, loses through the lower WEST price. P2 offsets part of the loss. ny_gas_basis_usd of +3 lowers the P4 payoff. Load is held at 1.0, so the loss comes from congestion, zone volume and the WEST leg rather than from demand. This mix differs from earlier scenarios because the WEST leg works against the book.

The load increase adds to P5, and P2 offsets part of the spread loss. ny_gas_basis_usd of +4 reduces the P4 payoff. WEST on-peak and DART are unchanged. The estimate combines the spread and load sensitivities from the 5-day winter run, scaled linearly, and is uncertain.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: A nine-day pocket gas squeeze. Henry Hub rises 90% as LNG export pull and storage draws coincide with a pipeline maintenance outage, and in-city gas-fired units are constrained at the margin. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 200 $/MWh on each shocked day, below the 503.7 $/MWh winter implausibility threshold and close to the Elliott-type level of 338.5 $/MWh. P5, the short 140 MW N.Y.C. obligation hedged with a long WEST position, is the main loser. P2's long spread offsets part of that loss. ny_gas_basis_usd of +2 lowers the P4 call payoff slightly. Load and WEST on-peak are held neutral, so the loss comes only from the congestion and zone-volume channel. The estimate is a linear extrapolation of the 5-day winter sensitivities and is uncertain.

analogue.source: NYISO analogue table, Winter Storm Elliott

scenario.narrative: A long, mild-gas but high-load winter period over 20 days. Henry Hub rises only 40% because storage is adequate, but a persistent cold regime lifts N.Y.C. peak load to 1.12 of a typical winter day, which enlarges the short retail obligation in P5 each day. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 95 $/MWh on each shocked day, a moderate level well below the 400.6 $/MWh winter maximum. Over 20 days the spread drives most of the loss through P5, and the extra load adds a further increment. P2 offsets part of the spread loss. ny_gas_basis_usd of +1 has a negligible effect on P4. WEST on-peak and DART are unchanged, so P1 and P3 contribute little. The load effect is scaled from the 5-day winter sensitivity and is uncertain.

analogue.source: NYISO analogue table, January 2025 cold (NYISO)

scenario.narrative: A pipeline-constrained pocket squeeze over 10 days with a real-time price shortfall in upstate. Henry Hub rises 150% and in-city gas units are short of fuel, so the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 180 $/MWh each day. Real-time WEST clears 40% below day-ahead on shocked days, which helps the short-DART position P3 but lowers the value of the long WEST swap P1 and the long WEST leg of P5. Net effect: P5 and P1 losses dominate the gains from P3 and P2. ny_gas_basis_usd of +5 lowers the P4 payoff. Load is held at 1.0, so the loss comes from supply, congestion and real-time WEST pricing rather than demand. The estimate is a linear extrapolation of the winter sensitivities and carries the most uncertainty of the three.

analogue.source: NYISO analogue table, Winter Storm Elliott

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

TASK
Propose 3 distinct stress scenarios over a horizon of at most 30 days in which the book below loses at least $5,000,000 (a loss means negative total P&L).
Driver family: gas_supply
Season: winter


INPUTS
Context (units: prices $/MWh, gas $/MMBtu, power MW, time days):
{
 "active_positions": [
  "P1",
  "P2",
  "P3",
  "P4",
  "P5",
  "P6"
 ],
 "book": [
  {
   "channel": "system",
   "gains_when": "the WEST on-peak price is above K1",
   "loses_when": "the WEST on-peak price is below K1",
   "position": "P1",
   "what": "Long 100 MW swap on the WEST on-peak price, strike K1 = 39.49 $/MWh, 16 h per on-peak weekday"
  },

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

Henry Hub rises 110% as LNG export pull and storage draws coincide with a maintenance outage. In-city gas units are constrained, so the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 280 $/MWh on each shocked day, below the 503.7 $/MWh winter implausibility threshold and close to the Elliott-type level of 338.5 $/MWh. P5 remains the main loser through the spread, and P2 offsets part of it. ny_gas_basis_usd of +3 lowers the P4 payoff. Load and DART are held neutral. The loss is a linear extrapolation of the 5-day winter sensitivities and is uncertain.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

scenario.narrative: Pipeline outages cut gas into the city for seven days. Henry Hub rises 90%, and the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by 240 $/MWh on each shocked day. Real-time WEST also clears 80% above day-ahead on the same days because scarce gas and ramping limits push real-time prices up. The DART move hurts P3, which receives day-ahead minus real-time at WEST off-peak, and adds to the loss. The main loss still comes from P5 through the spread, partly offset by P2. P1 gains somewhat from the higher real-time WEST level, which reduces the net. ny_gas_basis_usd of +3 lowers the P4 payoff. Load is held at 1.0. The estimate is a linear extrapolation of the 5-day winter sensitivities and is uncertain.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

The pocket stays tight while WEST clears on its normal summer path. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $80/MWh on every day for 30 days, which is the main adverse channel. The 1,500 MW shortfall is set at the near-term low end of the stated range. Load_peak_ratio is held at 1.0 because a shortfall cannot raise load. Gas, DART and WEST on-peak levels are unchanged to isolate the congestion channel. Confidence is low: the causal link from a large-load shortfall to a persistent Zone J spread widening is weak and the magnitude is an assumption. Losses come from the short retail obligation P5 (140 MW, 24 h), partly offset by the long spread position P2.

scenario.narrative: Large-load shortfall: about 1,000 MW of expected large-load demand is absent for 30 days, so upstate and WEST on-peak demand and the marginal price fall sharply relative to plan. WEST on-peak prices drop by 80% against the unshocked path, which hurts the long WEST swap P1 (100 MW) and the long heat-rate call P4 (50 MW). The short-volume position P6 gains as its strike is not reached. At the same time the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $40/MWh because NYC supply margins stay tight while WEST prices fall. Load_peak_ratio is held at 1.0 because a shortfall cannot raise load. The 80% WEST move is inside the summer historical minimum of -88.5% and above the implausible floor of -90.8%, but it is at the extreme end. Confidence is low, since a sustained 30-day WEST collapse with a widening NYC spread is a stressed combination rather than an observed event.

Large-load shortfall over a 10-day window: about 500 MW of large-load arrivals slip past the summer planning date, leaving the N.Y.C. pocket with less new supply than the forward curve assumed. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $210/MWh on each of the 10 days, which is the dominant loss channel because the short retail obligation P5 (140 MW, 24 h) is exposed to pocket prices with no offsetting hedge beyond the 25 MW spread position P2. WEST on-peak falls by 20% as upstate prices soften, costing P1 and P4 modestly. Load_peak_ratio is held at 1.0 and the shortfall is at the near-high end of the stated range. The $210 spread is below the summer historical maximum of $289.7 and under the implausible ceiling of $363.1. Confidence is low: the spread magnitude is a scenario assumption and the physical link from a modest large-load shortfall to a 10-day pocket spread widening is not established.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.

Over 30 days the N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $70/MWh each day because the pocket must run older local units and cannot import cheap upstate energy beyond transmission limits. WEST on-peak, gas and DART are left unchanged so the loss isolates the zone-volume channel that drives the short 140 MW retail obligation P5, partly offset by the long spread position P2. Load_peak_ratio is held at 1.0 because a shortfall cannot raise load. The $70 spread is inside the summer historical maximum of $289.7 and well under the implausible ceiling of $363.1. Confidence is low because the persistence of a 30-day pocket spread widening from a modest shortfall is an assumption.

Large-load shortfall with a combined congestion and system leg: about 900 MW of expected large-load demand is absent for 30 days, so upstate demand that was meant to support WEST prices softens and Henry Hub loosens. WEST on-peak falls 30% against the unshocked path, which costs the long swap P1 and the heat-rate call P4, while Henry Hub falls 20% over the same window, adding a second loss on P1 and P4 through the power-gas link. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $55/MWh each day because the pocket keeps its local gas-fired units while upstate prices reprice lower, the main loss on the short retail obligation P5, partly offset by the long spread position P2. Load_peak_ratio is held at 1.0. The WEST move of -30% and gas move of -20% are both inside the summer historical ranges, and the spread is well under the implausible ceiling. Confidence is low because the joint three-channel move is a stressed assumption rather than an observed event.

Large-load shortfall concentrated in a 12-day operational stress window: about 1,500 MW of large-load arrivals slip well beyond the Gold Book near-term low case, so N.Y.C. reliability margins are thin and operators rely on fast units and extra reserves. The N.Y.C. minus WEST spread widens by $180/MWh on each of the 12 days, which is the dominant loss channel for the short retail obligation P5 with only the 25 MW spread position P2 as an offset. Real-time clears 150% above day-ahead on the same days as the reserve-driven rebalancing pushes real-time prices up, which hurts the DART position P3 and the short call P6. WEST on-peak and gas are unchanged so the loss is isolated to the pocket and the DART channel. Load_peak_ratio is held at 1.0 because a shortfall cannot raise load. The $180 spread is under the summer historical maximum of $289.7 and the 150% DART move is under the summer historical maximum of 207.8%. Confidence is low because the DART premium over 12 days is an assumption.

CONSTRAINTS
- Hourly prices are clipped at a scenario cap of $5,000/MWh (a stated assumption of this exercise, not a NYISO rule); spike_daily_avg_usd is a daily on-peak average, so it also cannot exceed this.
- duration_days cannot exceed horizon_days; spike_days cannot exceed duration_days.
- spike_daily_avg_usd must be 0 when spike_days is 0 and positive otherwise.
- Shocks must be directionally consistent with the driver class (a cold snap raises load and gas, a heat wave raises load).
- Shock key mapping (agent key = internal key): ref_onpeak_pct = wh_onpeak_pct (WEST on-peak move), pocket_minus_ref_usd = dom_minus_wh_usd (N.Y.C. minus WEST, $/MWh), large_load_shock_mw = dc_load_shock_mw.
- Set stated_loss_usd to your own estimate of the book loss in USD (a number); it is compared with the engine's loss.
- Use numbers only (no ranges, no strings) for every shock. Use only the allowed enum values.
- If you cite an analogue, every claimed number must come from the analogue table and be within 30% of it. If no table entry fits, leave the analogue event empty and set confidence to low.

METHOD
1. State the causal chain from the physical driver to prices to the book's P&L.
2. Choose shock sizes that are extreme but plausible, and keep them mutually consistent.
3. Use different channels (system level, congestion, day-ahead vs real-time, gas, zone volume, tail) across your scenarios.
4. If the context has a 'book' table, read it with 'book_summary' and 'shock_glossary': pick shocks that hurt the positions that lose money (not shocks that only raise prices and gas, which make long positions gain), use 'shock_sensitivities' (if present) to see which shock moves which position and by how much, and stay inside 'shock_ceilings_by_season' (beyond implausible_above or below implausible_below a scenario is classed implausible).
5. Use the given driver family as driver_class and the given season as season in every scenario.
6. Signs must match the driver family (hard rule sign_consistent): for large_load_shortfall, large_load_shock_mw must be zero or negative and load_peak_ratio at most 1.0; for cold_snap and heat_wave, load_peak_ratio at least 1.0; for cold_snap and gas_supply, gas_hh_pct at least 0.
7. After each round you will receive engine numbers and rule verdicts only. Move shocks toward scenarios that breach the loss target with the smallest historical implausibility (small D^2, q at least 0.1%) and change direction when a rule fails.
